paper_metadata.title: Quantum Stochastic Walks for Portfolio Optimization: Theory and Implementation on Financial Networks

summary: The paper studies a quantum stochastic walk (QSW) portfolio optimizer on the Top-100 U.S. equities universe and a 625-point parameter grid, both simulated on an NVIDIA A100 GPU with cuPyNumeric. QSW improves turnover dramatically versus mean-variance optimization (e.g., 2% vs. 482% annual turnover in the best 1-year scenario; 36% vs. 351% median turnover across 50 random universes), but it does not demonstrate practical gate-based quantum advantage and loses on Sharpe in the 2-year setting (about 1.02-1.05 for QSW vs. 1.30 for MPT).

experiments.description: GPU-accelerated quantum stochastic walk (QSW) portfolio optimization on the Top-100 U.S. equities universe, evaluated under six hand-designed parameter scenarios across two training windows and five quantum-classical mixing values.

algorithm.variant: quantum stochastic walk (QSW) portfolio optimizer with dual-channel coherent + stochastic dynamics
algorithm.parameter_initialization: rho(0)=I/n (uniform mixed state); scenario parameters set by predefined presets

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Assets are nodes in a weighted directed graph; portfolio weights are extracted from the stationary diagonal of the density matrix. No qubit-based encoding is described because the implementation is classical/GPU simulation of QSW dynamics.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Maximize risk-adjusted return and diversification by evolving a density matrix under a QSW whose stationary distribution defines portfolio weights; graph weights use exp(alpha*SR_j - beta*Sigma_ij) off-diagonal and exp(lambda*SR_i) on-diagonal.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Long-only, fully invested portfolio with weights normalized to sum to 1; diversification emerges from the stochastic channel rather than explicit penalty constraints.
problem_formulation.problem_hamiltonian: H_ii = -gamma1*SR_i; H_ij = gamma2*Sigma_hat_ij for i != j

problem_instance.description: Portfolio optimization over the 100 largest U.S. equities by market capitalization, with quarterly rebalancing and backtesting over 2018-01-02 to 2024-12-31.
problem_instance.dataset_name: Yahoo Finance U.S. large-cap equities / Top-100 S&P constituents

ticker_symbols: Top 100 U.S. equities by market cap (examples listed: AAPL, MSFT, GOOGL, AMZN, NVDA, JPM, BAC, WFC, JNJ, UNH, PFE)
dataset_specification.preprocessing: daily adjusted close prices -> log returns; compute sample mean, volatility, covariance; annualize metrics for evaluation
dataset_specification.train_test_split: rolling 1-year and 2-year look-back windows; out-of-sample backtest from 2018-01-02 to 2024-12-31

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Daily adjusted closing prices were converted to log returns; sample covariance matrix S computed from training window; mean returns, volatilities, and Sharpe ratios computed per asset; covariance normalized for Hamiltonian construction.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Scenario analysis across 6 parameter presets x 5 omega values, evaluated under 1-year and 2-year rolling training windows with quarterly rebalancing; performance compared against MPT maximum-Sharpe and S&P 500 benchmarks.

implementation_details.classical_solver: PyPortfolioOpt for MPT benchmark; QSW implemented with GPU-accelerated linear algebra
implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Compute returns, covariance, Sharpe ratios, and graph weights from historical prices
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Extract portfolio weights from stationary density matrix diagonal and normalize to sum to 1
implementation_details.total_execution_time: ~3 hours for full 625-parameter grid on a single NVIDIA A100 GPU (reported for the grid-search experiment; scenario runs are included in the same implementation stack)

speedup_claims.caveats: This is an efficiency ratio improvement, not a computational speedup.
Implementation-cost advantage, not algorithmic runtime speedup.
Net-of-cost advantage emphasized; raw Sharpe may be lower than MPT.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: O(n^3) for matrix exponentials; O(n^2) for transition-rate operations; diagonal extraction O(n)
complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: Not explicitly characterized beyond classical mean-variance optimization and GPU linear algebra; MPT benchmark solved with PyPortfolioOpt
complexity_analysis.wall_clock_quantum: ~3 hours for 625-parameter grid on one NVIDIA A100 GPU

advantage_assessment.crossover_size: not reported; no quantum-classical crossover analysis
advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: No quantum hardware resources demonstrated; implementation is a classical GPU simulation on NVIDIA A100 with cuPyNumeric
limiting_factors: No gate-based quantum circuit or QPU execution
Classical MPT benchmark outperforms QSW on 2-year training windows (Sharpe 1.30 vs. 1.02-1.05)
The reported implementation is GPU-accelerated classical simulation, not quantum hardware
No constant-factor or crossover analysis supporting practical quantum advantage

notes: This is a gate-based-scope paper only in the broad quantum-computing sense, but the reported implementation is a classical/GPU simulation of QSW dynamics rather than a circuit executed on qubits. Therefore num_qubits and circuit-depth fields are null because no qubit register or circuit is specified.
hardware.type inferred as simulator_other because the paper reports GPU-accelerated cuPyNumeric implementation on NVIDIA A100, not a QPU or annealer.
The paper reports QSW beating MPT on Sharpe for 1-year training windows, but losing on Sharpe for 2-year windows while always improving turnover and concentration.
Because the implementation is a classical GPU simulation rather than a gate-based quantum device, this does not establish practical quantum advantage.

algorithm.parameter_initialization: For each draw, run the full grid search from rho(0)=I/n and choose the best-performing configuration

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Graph-based QSW portfolio construction on each random 100-stock universe; no qubit encoding described.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Assess whether the best QSW configuration generalizes across random universes while maintaining high Sharpe, low turnover, and low concentration.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Long-only, fully invested; weights normalized to sum to 1.
problem_formulation.problem_hamiltonian: H_ii = -gamma1*SR_i; H_ij = gamma2*Sigma_hat_ij for i != j

problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: 50 replications; 31,350 back-tests total (50 x (625 + 2)); report medians, distributions, win rates, and parameter histograms.
